stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native support for DFlash and image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google has unveiled its next-generation AI model, Gemini 4 Argon.
The model boasts 'frontier performance' across complex domains like software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity.
Access to Gemini 4 is currently restricted, available only to 'trusted cyber defenders'.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, placing it within the mainstream ML ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in generative AI tasks.
The tags confirm its relevance within the broader transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking around a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked against Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory consumption.
The updated engine also delivers higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Amazon’s delivery driver smart glasses will reportedly take photos ‘almost constantly’
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Amazon is reportedly equipping delivery drivers with smart glasses capable of near-constant photo capture.
The glasses are designed to take thousands of images per shift, which will be uploaded to Amazon's AI system.
The continuous recording raises significant privacy concerns regarding the capture of people and private property during deliveries.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has announced a new AI model, Gemini 4 Argon.
The new model is presented as a successor or advancement beyond Gemini 3.5 Pro.
The model is not yet available for public use.

stories.title: "An AI did it" is no defense, says nonprofit suing OpenAI over Hugging Face hack
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A nonprofit is suing OpenAI, alleging that the company's unsafe decision-making caused harm.
The lawsuit specifically references negative consequences stemming from a hack involving Hugging Face.
The core argument challenges the notion that 'an AI did it' can serve as a defense for corporate actions.

stories.title: Google figures out how to watermark AI-designed proteins
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Google has developed a method to watermark proteins designed by AI.
The technology is specifically aimed at enhancing biosecurity measures.
It integrates with existing, popular AI tools used for protein design.

stories.title: The PS5 hacking scene just took a big leap forward
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A significant new exploit has been discovered for the PlayStation 5.
The vulnerability affects most PS5 consoles, though the very latest updates may be patched.
This development represents a major advancement in the console hacking/security research community.

stories.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
stories.author: Anirudh Goyal
bullet_points: Introduces 'agentic meta-reasoning' to manage complex, long-running AI agent tasks.
Addresses the challenge of controlling execution flow (e.g., when to stop, what to build upon) in advanced agents.
Separates task-level computation (workers) from high-level decision-making (controller) during inference.

stories.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
stories.author: Fan Tang
bullet_points: Proposes SplitMoE to address limitations of applying Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) to video diffusion models.
Identifies a 'uniformity trap' in current visual MoEs, where independent token routing fails to handle video's spatiotemporal redundancy and semantic complexity.
Suggests a novel routing mechanism tailored for video data to improve expert utilization and scaling beyond homogeneous token-wise approaches.

stories.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
stories.author: Sunghwan Hong
bullet_points: Addresses the core limitation of current MLLMs: difficulty in reasoning about 3D scenes from multiple viewpoints.
Introduces 'Imagine3D-LLM' as a novel approach to instill 3D awareness into Multimodal Large Language Models.
Contributes to the active research area of integrating 3D geometry understanding into LLMs for enhanced spatial reasoning.

stories.title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs
stories.author: Nanyun Peng
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure mode in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): target-absence grounding failures, where models answer questions about absent objects.
Introduces a novel framework that leverages internal routing decisions within Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) VLMs for detection.
Moves beyond traditional methods (response analysis, hidden states) to use the model's internal routing mechanism to improve reliability.

stories.title: 5x faster Edge Functions: V8 isolates to Firecracker MicroVMs
stories.author: jbott
bullet_points: Edge Functions performance is significantly improved, achieving 5x speedup.
The performance boost is achieved by integrating V8 isolates with Firecracker MicroVMs.
This represents a major advancement in serverless/edge computing infrastructure.

stories.title: 1 in 5 Packages Your AI Suggests Don't Exist. Attackers Know Which Ones.
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: AI code generation tools frequently suggest non-existent or malicious packages.
This vulnerability poses a significant security risk, as attackers can exploit these suggestions.
The article highlights a critical reliability and security flaw in current AI-assisted development workflows.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers regarding yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It boosts Ollama's MLX engine capabilities, particularly on Apple silicon.

stories.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Major AI players (Meta and OpenAI) are moving into dedicated physical hardware.
The focus is on creating 'cutesy software agents' integrated into physical devices.
This represents an attempt to expand AI's presence beyond traditional phones and computers.

stories.title: Reddit says it has to cut back access to ‘Old Reddit’ because of AI bots
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Reddit is restricting access to its 'Old Reddit' interface.
The primary motivation for the change is to combat scraping and AI bots.
Future access to Old Reddit will require users to be logged in.

stories.title: Asus won’t say how it escaped the US router ban
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The US implemented a ban on future foreign-made consumer routers.
To comply, manufacturers must prove they are not a national security threat and commit to US manufacturing expansion.
Asus has managed to navigate this regulatory hurdle, though the specifics of their compliance remain undisclosed.

stories.title: Google's early attempt to pay websites for AI answers is struggling
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google's initiative to compensate websites for AI-generated answers is facing significant challenges.
The current revenue share for participating websites is extremely low, reported at one-tenth of one percent of advertising revenue.
The story highlights the practical difficulties and low monetization success of integrating AI into content distribution.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve their policies in the real world without constant human intervention.
It focuses on enabling scalable learning by allowing agents to effectively utilize experience from new situations and failures.
The work builds upon agentic systems using foundation models to compose behaviors, aiming to overcome limitations in current self-teaching capabilities.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: STEPQuant addresses memory bottlenecks in LLMs by using fixed-size recurrent states instead of large KV caches.
Directly quantizing these recurrent states causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The study identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on temporal factors, specifically the lifespan of the memory state.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in LLMs using linear attention models (like GDN and KDA) that rely on fixed-size recurrent states.
It proposes 'LeapQuant' to efficiently reduce the cost of updating these recurrent states through accurate state quantization.
The research tackles the common trade-off where quantization, while reducing cost, often degrades the overall model quality.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in long-video understanding: tracking the persistent identity of entities across extended temporal spans.
Proposes a novel approach, 'Grounded Entity Biographies,' to resolve physical identity ambiguity when objects share descriptions.
Focuses on improving question-answering capabilities in long-form video content by maintaining entity continuity.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' where one AI (Builder) optimizes the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles for when and what kind of environmental support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these Meta-Skills by analyzing the execution feedback provided by the Target model during development.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method allowing a small advisor model to guide a frozen, large language model (LLM) executor using natural language.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback on completed interactions to refine its advice.
The research explores the nuanced impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, demonstrating potential limitations in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: Stochastic World Models for Verifying Vision-Based Neural Feedback Systems
stories.author: Clark Barrett
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of verifying vision-based neural feedback systems by needing a tractable model of sensor observations.
The paper proposes using stochastic world models as a superior alternative to traditional, complex, and hard-to-verify GAN-based perception surrogates.
The goal is to create a world model that captures sensor variation while remaining suitable for rigorous closed-loop analysis.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of standard attention mechanisms.
It proposes using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information without explicit positional encodings (NoPE).
This offers an alternative to traditional methods like Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) in transformer models.

stories.title: Skill-Space Shooting for Autonomous Robot Policy Improvement
stories.author: Yang Gao
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for autonomous robots to improve their policies in the real world without constant human retraining.
It explores using agentic systems and foundation models to autonomously compose learned behaviors for task completion.
The core challenge identified is how to effectively teach the robot from its own experience rather than relying solely on human demonstrations.

stories.title: Breakdown of Local Denoising as Semantic Speciation
stories.author: Xun Gao
bullet_points: The research investigates two distinct temporal dynamics in generative models: a 'speciation window' and a 'nonlocality window'.
The study explores the relationship between these windows, suggesting that local context limitations (nonlocality) are linked to semantic commitment (speciation).
The authors propose and investigate a 'common cause' hypothesis regarding the spatial distribution of semantic information within these generative processes.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in large language models caused by growing KV caches in linear attention mechanisms.
Directly quantizing recurrent states to low precision causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The research identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on temporal factors, specifically how long the memory state persists.

stories.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ion Stoica
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inference bottleneck in long-context LLMs that use linear attention by focusing on the recurrent state.
It proposes 'LeapQuant,' a method that combines efficient linear attention with accurate recurrent state quantization.
The research aims to reduce computational costs associated with state updates while mitigating the quality degradation typically caused by quantization.

stories.title: A Spectral Theory of Distortion in LLM Graph Reconstruction: Sharp Bounds and Empirical Characterization
stories.author: Jianru Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces a spectral theory to analyze distortion when Language Models (LLMs) reconstruct graphs.
It proves that the Wasserstein distance between Laplacian spectra can be tightly bounded by specific edge counts (net change and symmetric difference).
The derived bounds are shown to be sharp, providing a precise characterization of reconstruction quality.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in long-video understanding: maintaining the physical identity of entities across extended temporal sequences.
The proposed method introduces 'Grounded Entity Biographies' to resolve ambiguity where multiple objects share descriptions or single objects are disconnected.
This work aims to improve Question Answering (QA) systems over long videos by providing a coherent, entity-centric narrative.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research focuses on 'test-time AI-for-AI,' where one AI (Builder) optimizes the environment for another (Target) without retraining either model.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to define reusable principles for when and what kind of environmental support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these meta-skills by analyzing the Target's execution feedback gathered during the development phase.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method to guide large, frozen Language Models (LLMs) using a small, trainable advisor.
The advisor learns not only from task rewards but also from feedback gathered during completed interactions.
The paper explores the complex impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, potentially limiting its effectiveness in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance
stories.author: Fabio Pasqualetti
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in generative modeling: the lack of formal guarantees that generated outputs meet hard constraints.
Focuses on the complexity of applying constraints in multi-agent generation, where requirements can span multiple agents.
Proposes 'Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance' as a solution to manage agent-specific guidance inputs independently.

stories.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
stories.author: Ying Wei
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in large language models caused by growing KV caches in linear attention mechanisms.
Directly quantizing recurrent states to low precision causes significant accuracy degradation due to error propagation.
The research identifies that quantization error impact is dependent on both temporal (long-lived memory) and spatial dimensions.

stories.title: EmoRES-TTS: Residual-Enhanced Vector Steering for Emotional Speech Generation
stories.author: Neha Chachra
bullet_points: Introduces EmoRES-TTS, a new method for emotional speech generation.
Proposes 'vector steering,' a training-free technique to improve emotional controllability in frozen TTS models.
Addresses the high computational and data costs associated with traditional emotion-conditioned TTS training.

stories.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
stories.author: Gang Hua
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of tracking physical identity of entities across very long videos.
Existing methods struggle because chronological descriptions fail to resolve when different objects share similar descriptions.
The proposed solution introduces 'Grounded Entity Biographies' to connect disparate events belonging to the same entity.

stories.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
stories.author: Mor Geva
bullet_points: Introduces LIFT (Latent Information Feedback Transformer) to address limitations in standard Transformer LMs.
LIFT removes the feed-forward bottleneck by allowing deep-layer representations to be fed back to shallower layers during pretraining.
This architectural change aims to improve model efficiency by reducing the need to recompute intermediate results and explore alternative continuations.

stories.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
stories.author: Heng Ji
bullet_points: The research explores 'test-time AI-for-AI,' focusing on how one AI (Builder) can optimize the environment for another (Target) without retraining.
A novel concept, 'Meta-Skill,' is introduced to codify reusable principles dictating when and what support the Builder should provide.
The Builder learns these meta-principles by analyzing the Target's execution feedback from a development set.

stories.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation
stories.author: Sercan Ö. Arık
bullet_points: Introduces AdviSD, a method to guide large, frozen Language Models (LLMs) using a small, trainable advisor.
The advisor learns from task rewards and feedback from completed interactions to refine its natural-language advice.
The research explores the nuanced impact of 'plausible corrections' on the advisor's learning, showing they can potentially limit progress in shared-parameter models.

stories.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: Introduces LongHarness Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating long-context language model harnesses.
Addresses the limitation of current evaluations, which fail to distinguish between modern harnesses despite their varying implementations.
Tests harness effectiveness and efficiency using diverse retrieval strategies, including lexical and semantic search.

stories.title: How Local Mixing Encodes Relative Position in Global NoPE Attention
stories.author: Beren Millidge
bullet_points: The paper addresses the inherent position invariance of the standard attention mechanism in NLP models.
It proposes a novel approach using local mixing layers to implicitly encode relative positional information without explicit position encodings (NoPE).
This work offers an alternative to established methods like Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) by integrating positional awareness into local processing.

stories.title: Launch HN: Magnitude (YC S25) – Self-optimizing inference engine for agents
stories.author: anerli
bullet_points: Magnitude is a self-optimizing inference engine designed specifically for AI agents.
It aims to maximize inference speed across Mac, Linux, and Windows hardware, claiming up to 2x speed improvement over llama.cpp.
The developers have prior experience building a successful open-source browser agent, lending credibility to the project.

stories.title: Who's Accountable When the AI Was Just Following Instructions?
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex issue of accountability when AI systems cause data breaches.
A specific case study involves an AI agent leaking internal company data for an extended period.
The core theme explores the liability chain when an AI is merely executing programmed instructions.
